children: The BSE Sensex jumps 1,533.72 points to settle at 74,315.61. The NSE Nifty50 advances 1.66 per cent, to close at 22,997
Indian equity markets staged a strong recovery on Thursday, with the Sensex and Nifty posting sharp gains despite weakness across global markets.

Buying interest in information technology, automobile and private banking stocks, alongside Reliance Industries, lifted the benchmarks, while the announcement of the Jio Platforms IPO added to investor interest.
The markets opened on a subdued note but gathered momentum as the session progressed, with the Sensex ending close to its intraday high and the Nifty50 finishing just short of the 23,000 mark.
The BSE Sensex jumped 1,533.72 points, or 2.11 per cent, to settle at 74,315.61. The NSE Nifty50 advanced 374.65 points, or 1.66 per cent, to close at 22,997.35.

However, the rally was not broad-based. The Nifty Midcap index fell 0.5 per cent, while the Nifty Smallcap index declined 1.3 per cent, indicating continued pressure on smaller companies even as heavyweight stocks drove the benchmarks higher.

“Indian equities rallied sharply as concerns over stretched AI valuations and higher US inflation triggered a sell-off across tech-heavy global markets, improving India’s relative appeal and encouraging rotation toward domestic large-cap technology, private financials and defensive heavyweights. Correcting bond yields, rupee stability and softening crude prices further supported sentiment,” said Vinod Nair, Head of Research, Geojit Investments.
IT, Banking, Telecom Stocks Rally
Tech Mahindra, ICICI Bank, Bharti Airtel, HCL Technologies and Reliance Industries emerged among the leading Nifty50 gainers.

Sectorally, automobile, IT, infrastructure, oil and gas, private banking and realty indices advanced between 1 per cent and 1.8 per cent. In contrast, media and public sector banking indices fell by more than 1 per cent each.
On the losing side, Nestle India, Trent, Adani Enterprises, Shriram Finance and Larsen & Toubro featured among the key laggards on the Nifty50.

Among individual stocks, Yes Bank suffered one of the sharpest declines, with its shares tumbling 14 per cent after the Supreme Court rejected the write-off of Rs 8,415 crore worth of additional tier-1 (AT-1) bonds.
IDBI Bank shares dropped 8 per cent after Fairfax Financial Holdings-backed Canada Inc. emerged as a potential stakeholder in the lender.
HDB Financial Services fell 7 per cent despite reporting a profit for the second quarter, as investors appeared unconvinced by the results.

Bajaj Consumer Care shares declined more than 10 per cent despite the company reporting a quarterly profit. CEAT also came under pressure, falling over 4 per cent even after posting a 39.8 per cent increase in profit.

Aeroflex Industries shed 10 per cent following the announcement of a capacity expansion programme. MRPL shares dropped nearly 6 per cent, notwithstanding a 203 per cent year-on-year surge in second-quarter profit.
Hathway Cable & Datacom declined 6.7 per cent after reporting a fall in quarterly profit.
Among the notable gainers outside the benchmark heavyweights, Cemindia Projects advanced 5 per cent following the launch of QOP.
NIIT shares rose 1.2 per cent after the company appointed Anish Sarkar as its chief executive officer.

Thursday's session highlighted the divergence between large-cap stocks and the broader market. While strong buying in heavyweight companies propelled the Sensex and Nifty higher, weakness in mid-cap and small-cap shares, alongside sharp declines in several individual stocks, suggested that investor confidence remained selective.
